review: Reviewed all 434 source formula occurrences and their 437 interpretations against the source and original Lean contexts. Carriers, real embeddings, metric instances, bounded metrics, open-subspace reciprocal-distance metrics, dependent disjoint unions, product sums, Baire constructions and both Alexandrov directions preserve the source constructions and hypotheses. Sequence indices start at zero; finite dimension levels remain distinct from recursive dimension indices. Source-owned binders retain lexical identity, actual proof-local definitions and subtype inclusions. Distance-to-set, diameter, summability and defining-equality requirements retain their kernel-checked premises. Numeric limits take their type from the source sequence. The shared initial zero retains both Bool.false and Nat.zero and is checked against the argument actually used in each cylinder proof. The Anderson/Anderson--Kadec consequence remains conditional on explicit external homeomorphism assumptions. Interpretation approval is distinct from expression typing, operator inspection and the truth of an arbitrary displayed formula. Native-core migration review: structural token refinement, convergence candidates, aligned displays, expression lists, literal natural lower bounds, finite/infinite/tail summation bodies, predicate-set generators, typed identity-singleton families, generated metric-ball families, natural-indexed product/disjoint-union/set-family candidates and their exact lower-bound/lexical-index spans, original-identity context-prefix checks, lexical/decorated-name occurrence extraction, unsupported set-builder guards, complete grammar-owned binding-effect registration, explicit outer source-to-Lean variable/constant resolution with occurrence selectors and subtype/index checks, local lexical overrides with hygienic names and source-domain inheritance, post-resolution carrier/family-kind/lower-bound/convergence-origin checks in one native variable-resolution pipeline, source binding/target normalization and proof-context/declaration inventory validation, literal/numeral/predicate/premise-source and scope-interval validation, complete raw annotation scanning with duplicate-key and integer-token JSON auditing, explicit literal/numeric-domain/rational-ambient/prefix-predicate normalization, forward bounded-trace premise matching with ambiguity rejection, comparison numeral normalization and source-typed real/extended-nonnegative-real operand coercion, and the registered recognizers run in Haskell. Multidigit power bases remain one operand; unsupported integer arithmetic and unreviewed exponent domains remain rejected. Kernel tests reject changed endpoints, power bases/instances and exponent domains while preserving the original dimension-bound APIs and real sequence coordinates. Expression jobs retain their root/nested distinction; nested map arrows cannot manufacture new binders. Kernel tests reject map-domain substitutions, missing defining-equality proofs and wrong empty-set domains/instances, and preserve distinct nested sequence indices. Sequence interpretation requires resolved local-binder identities from the native resolver; nested shadowed indices remain distinct and domain/index substitutions remain rejected by kernel evidence checks. Unregistered constants remain unsupported rather than receiving guessed declarations. Set operands retain source order and spans, while membership records Lean operands in set/point order and derives its point adapter, domain and instance independently from the source set. Indexed carrier calls retain all repeated-call checks. Unregistered chains and ungrouped set products remain rejected; targeted kernel tests reject changed set domains, instances, points and carrier copies. Source-classified set-distance evaluation and subtype-range lowering also use the shared AST renderer. Set-distance preserves the independent metric carrier/instance and point/set operands; its nonemptiness requirement remains kernel checked. Subtype-range requires the exact source predicate of the function domain, retains independent function/domain/codomain expectations, and traverses decorated callees once rather than emitting an unused duplicate marker. Kernel tests reject substituted domain sets and missing point-membership evidence, and retain unresolved nonemptiness obligations when no evidence exists. Targeted Lean tests reject wrong scoped callees, swapped arguments, substituted metrics and missing point-membership evidence. Reindexing retains the original source operand span, the target index expression and its declared origin. Source-preserving integer-exponent tokenization and two-branch case normalization with hygienic proof names also run in Haskell. Ordinary terms, instrumented terms, contexts and ordered operand traces match the reviewed interpreter; targeted kernel tests reject wrong comparison instances, swapped arguments, incorrect indices and unsupported exponent arithmetic. A single AST traversal generates ordinary and instrumented terms, source spans and ordered explicit/implicit operand expectations; domain witnesses come from AST source references rather than generated Lean strings. All 434 formulas, 437 interpretations and their operator traces match the previously reviewed interpreter. Wrong heads, swapped operands, incorrect implicit instances and interval coercions remain rejected. Candidate and Reviewed are distinct opaque types; review still requires source/rules/Lean fingerprint equality and cannot be granted by Lean success. Unregistered construction annotations remain explicit native failures; there is no production Python interpretation fallback. Python retains execution scheduling, Lean communication and caches. Source, Lean signatures/bodies and mathematical interpretations are unchanged. The typed semantic environment carries constants, bindings and conventions together. Typed-map kernel regressions preserve shadowing of an unrelated outer point and reject substituted subspace domains. Mixed equality/membership chains remain outside the generic equality rule. Family and tuple kernel regressions reject changed fibers, index types, subset predicates, ambient types, lattice operations and lower bounds. Full typed diagonal signatures and their defining tuples preserve the original lexical inputs and proof. Native family recognition continues to produce candidates; unsupported comprehension bodies remain explicit failures rather than losing obligations. Convergence and summation kernel regressions reject altered filters, limits, domains, upper/lower bounds and multiplication instances; summability remains a separate obligation and is unresolved for the divergent constant series. Ordinary-only type/domain witnesses share the original occupied-name environment. A collision regression for a coordinate-space limit preserves its free source carrier and is kernel-equal to the intended Tendsto statement. These tests preserve the original scoped contexts and subtype-inclusion requirements. Only the outermost source comparison consumes sentence punctuation. Regression and kernel checks preserve dependent metric families, subset point/set lifting, subspace domains and real division for Nat indices. They reject replaced metrics on the same carrier, changed topologies/carriers, reversed composition/restriction operands and absent boundedness/inclusion evidence. Source-domain comparison uses canonical identities in the semantic AST rather than generated Lean text; repeated indexed metrics retain their own operator and argument checks. Registered primed set references retain distance-to-set classification. Nested comprehensions and comprehensions in indexed sets and sums preserve source scopes and binder/delimiter positions. Infimum and defining-equality requirements remain separate kernel obligations. All existing chapter interpretations and traces remain identical. Outside that reviewed corpus, a previously rejected distance-to-comprehension combination now retains its set role and lowers to Metric.infDist. A kernel regression rejects the old point interpretation, leaves nonemptiness unresolved without evidence and proves the obligation only with the matching predicate-set evidence. No chapter source or Lean proof changed. Case and pair kernel regressions check the actual chapter definition directly through the native interpreter, reject duplicate conditions, changed cross-component values, reverse transport and wrong tags/families, and preserve the source Sigma construction and Eq.mp witness. Available original binder signatures are included in the expression-job cache key, while proof bodies stay in the separate context-replay layer rather than repeated semantic payloads. Source, Lean proofs and all existing interpretation traces remain unchanged. General comparisons retain original abstract source types; Lean verifies their order instances. Negative kernel evidence rejects changing the order instance and attempting an order comparison on Type-valued function results. Numeric-domain, literal-consumer and radius-bound annotations remain explicit source evidence rather than inferred defaults. All 437 chapter interpretation units are supported directly by the native semantic interpreter. Their ordinary/instrumented terms, contexts and ordered traces are identical to the independently selected original revision. Kernel regressions preserve inclusion/membership proofs, finite intersection endpoints, decreasing-family scopes, rational casts and generated predicates; changed domains, lattice instances, index ranges, boundedness guards and active metric bindings remain rejected or unresolved. The new finite union fold has an independent kernel equality to the intended indexed union and rejects an intersection lattice instance, reversed ranges, mixed operators and unregistered subtraction folds. Production chapter analysis accepts source text, explicit scopes/configuration and one original-signature table; scanning, shared parsing, normalization, lexical/domain resolution, expression splitting, context bridges and both renderings stay inside a single Haskell transaction. The old interpreter is confined to a frozen test-only oracle. Unregistered syntax and transport errors cannot select it. Operator candidates and nested inspection plans are also native and match the independently selected original revision for every source formula. Integration regressions preserve clause-local convergence binders, spacing in weighted metric applications, source diagnostic reasons, missing/unparsed/list fragments and source-typed literals. The full 366-test run passed 365 tests; its sole remaining test fixture omitted a source identity. That fixture now carries the original x binding and passes together with related failed-fragment and shared-literal checks. Production code stayed unchanged during that correction. The source-level transaction test prevents fine-grained Python normalization/walk/resolution calls, excludes declaration proof bodies from the wire and checks that exactly one chapter request produces the formula report. Shared-environment tests reject incompatible local-definition prefixes and retain independent cache responses. The canonical source and original Lean signatures/bodies are unchanged; all ordinary terms, instrumented terms, source contexts, ordered traces and visible operator candidates match the reviewed original interpreter. The common AST, chapter mapping plans and source derivation evidence have separate responsibilities. Typed coercions, ranges, singletons, indexed lambdas/aggregations, result-typed dependent conditionals, typed operator sections and literal type/witness evidence preserve the reviewed source operands and original contexts. Comparison-list expansion, shared membership and scalar witnesses annotate ordinary operations without replacing their Lean head, operands or obligations. Generated-family premise provenance retains the exact named source references, syntax and boundedness proof without requiring ball-specific fields in the common AST. Both renderings and ordered trace evidence agree with the reviewed interpretations. Semantic AST inspection is an opt-in read-only projection of the interpreted Haskell value; it preserves the ordinary rendering, instrumented rendering and all ordered source/operator evidence, and cannot submit or approve a replacement interpretation. Formula display tags use the shared source scanner and preserve source positions and both semantic renderings; PDF glyph tagging and overlay geometry do not change the mathematical interpretation or its kernel obligations. Original-source range inspection is a separate read-only action; the selected original interpreter comparison still agrees on all 434 formulas, 437 interpretations and 730 operator calls. Range matching requires the serialized complete kernel application, declaration and referenced local types/values; changed arguments, types, let values and ambiguous shadowed locals are rejected. It cannot approve or replace the interpreted expressions.
